milestone: Bell Laboratories visible speech instruments (sound spectrograph, cathode ray translator) were in use in an educational research program for the deaf.

name: Planets condensing from a nebula
milestone: Hubble Space Telescope resolved protoplanetary disks (proplyds) around young stars in the Orion Nebula (O'Dell, Wen, Hu 1993; O'Dell & Wen 1994).

milestone: Lockheed Martin and Edwards AFB tested a production-representative Automatic Ground Collision Avoidance System on an F-16.

name: Moving whole houses or towns
milestone: Old Katonah, New York, was relocated: about 55 houses, stores, barns and a church were moved to New Katonah ahead of the New Croton Dam reservoir.

name: Virtual clothing preview
reasons: best entry of a top-100 book
milestone: A 3D Virtual Fitting Room (MIRALab/FashionMe) let users see an animated virtual model walking in garments.

name: Electronic or digital wristwatch
milestone: Hamilton Pulsar went on sale, 18-carat gold, $2,100, red LED display

name: Non-metal firearm
reasons: best entry of a top-100 author
milestone: Defense Distributed fired the 3D-printed plastic Liberator pistol in early May 2013.

name: Clearing debris and obstacles from space lanes
milestone: The RemoveDEBRIS satellite (Surrey Space Centre-led, deployed from the ISS) captured a deployed simulated debris target in a net in orbit.

name: Fish and shellfish farming
reasons: best entry of a top-100 author
best entry of a top-100 book
milestone: First salmon farms established in Norway and Scotland in the late 1960s.

name: Eye-tracking interface
reasons: best entry of a top-100 author

milestone: Richard Bolt at MIT demonstrated 'Gaze-orchestrated dynamic windows', a display whose windows react to where the viewer looks (SIGGRAPH 1981).

best_entry.title: The Land of the Changing Sun

name: Delivery through the skin
reasons: best entry of a top-100 author
best entry of a top-100 book
milestone: The same angina treatment was used on 17 patients as routine clinical therapy.

name: Superconducting power conductor
milestone: Southwire energized a high-temperature superconducting power cable at its Carrollton, Georgia plant, feeding three plant facilities with liquid-nitrogen-cooled superconducting cable (18 Feb 2000).

name: Refracted-light ring around the Earth
milestone: Surveyor 3's TV camera on the Moon photographed the Earth eclipsing the Sun on 24 April 1967, showing a lighted ring of sunlight refracted around the dark Earth disc.

name: Accelerated aging and curing
milestone: Lost Spirits Distillery (California) reported a reactor that ages rum to a 20-year chemical profile in six days.

name: Physical basis of memory
milestone: Bliss and Lomo reported long-lasting potentiation of synaptic transmission in the rabbit dentate gyrus after perforant path stimulation (long-term potentiation).

best_entry.title: The Certainty of a Future Life in Mars

name: Baldness treatment
milestone: Norman Orentreich (New York) reported autografts of hair-bearing scalp into bald areas of male-pattern-baldness patients, showing the grafts kept growing.

name: Self-reconfiguring modular machines
milestone: Toshio Fukuda and Seiya Nakagawa (Nagoya University) published the dynamically reconfigurable robotic system (CEBOT), many cells that detach and combine autonomously to reorganize, with basic experimental results of the cell mechanism.

name: Large astrometric surveys of star positions
milestone: Gaia Data Release 1 gave positions, parallaxes and proper motions for about 2 million stars (plus positions of 1.1 billion).

name: Air taxi
milestone: Lucerne taximeter 'aero-taxi' service of the Compagnie Trans-Aerienne reported inaugurated.

best_entry.title: The Mummy! A Tale of the Twenty-Second Century

name: Supertall tower
milestone: The Eiffel Tower opened to the public nine days after the Exposition opened on 6 May 1889; nearly 30,000 visitors climbed the stairs to the top before the lifts began on 26 May.

name: Hybrid of different species
milestone: Thomas Fairchild, an English nurseryman, produced the first documented artificial plant hybrid ('Fairchild's Mule'), Dianthus caryophyllus x barbatus, by hand-pollinating a carnation with sweet william.

name: Phobos and Deimos, the two moons of Mars
milestone: Asaph Hall at the U.S. Naval Observatory found Deimos (first seen 11 Aug 1877) and Phobos (17 Aug) with the 26-inch refractor; announced 18-19 Aug.

name: Submarine air supply
milestone: Narcis Monturiol submerged Ictineo II and ran its chemical (zinc, manganese dioxide, potassium chlorate) engine; the reaction released oxygen and the vessel stayed down about seven and a half hours.

best_entry.title: The Description of a New World, Called the Blazing-World

name: Fireproof construction
milestone: William Strutt built a six-storey fire-resistant calico mill in Derby (1792-93) with brick arches and tile/plaster floors on cast-iron columns, the first of the 'fireproof' mills.

name: Eugenic breeding of humans
milestone: Same event: the community's committee approved parents and children were born under the program from 1869.

best_entry.title: An Essay on the Principle of Population

name: Nerve-attacking weapon
reasons: best entry of a top-100 author
best entry of a top-100 book
milestone: Taser Public Defender first marketed in March 1975 by Advanced Chemical Technology of Los Angeles; more than 1,000 sold by November 1975, a few to police, and used in holdups and by civilians.

name: Orbital rendezvous and docking
reasons: best entry of a top-100 book
milestone: Apollo 11 Lunar Module Eagle rendezvoused with and docked to Columbia in lunar orbit; crew and lunar samples transferred, returning to Earth.

name: Spacecraft thermal control and insulation
milestone: Vostok 1: Gagarin reported a cockpit temperature of 20 degrees during the flight.

name: Futuristic cosmetics
reasons: best entry of a top-100 book
milestone: 1988: topical minoxidil (Rogaine) was approved for treating hair loss and sold.

name: Reusable winged spaceplane or shuttle
reasons: best entry of a top-100 book
milestone: STS-5 (Columbia) was the first operational shuttle flight and deployed two commercial communications satellites.

name: Uncrewed cargo spacecraft
reasons: best entry of a top-100 book
milestone: Progress 1 launched on 1978-01-20 and docked automatically with Salyut 6.

name: Reentry heat protection
milestone: Discoverer 13's reentry capsule (with heat shield) came down from orbit and was recovered from the Pacific, the first object recovered from orbit; Vostok 1 followed on 1961-04-12 with the first crewed ablative shield.

name: Lab-grown or synthetic meat
reasons: best entry of a top-100 author
milestone: Cultured chicken from Eat Just was sold at restaurant 1880 in Singapore, the first commercial sale of cell-cultured meat.

name: Capsule parachute or sea-splashdown recovery
milestone: Vostok 1's capsule returned the first human from orbit and landed by parachute on land in the Saratov region where it was recovered.

name: Handheld medical analyzer
reasons: best entry of a top-100 author
milestone: Same event: the Glucometer was sold for home and clinical use.

name: Automatic body-cleaning machine
milestone: Sanyo showed its Ultrasonic Bath at Expo 70 in Osaka: an enclosed chamber that sprayed warm water jets, ultrasonic mist and massage, then dried the user with warm air in about 15 minutes.

best_entry.title: A Hundred Years Hence (The Expectations of an Optimist)

name: Spacecraft cruising at tens of miles per second
milestone: Luna 1 (launched 2 January 1959) became the first object to reach Earth escape velocity, about 11 km/s (7 miles per second), and entered a heliocentric orbit between the orbits of Earth and Mars.

name: Manufacturing in space vacuum
reasons: best entry of a top-100 book
milestone: Wake Shield Facility (STS-60) grew crystalline semiconductor thin films in the ultrahigh vacuum wake it created in orbit (University of Houston/NASA).

name: Electronic voting and vote counting
reasons: best entry of a top-100 book
milestone: Seven US counties switched to punched-card voting with computer tallying for the 1964 presidential election.

name: Flight data recorder
reasons: best entry of a top-100 author
milestone: General Mills marketed a Flight Recorder that etched heading, airspeed, acceleration and altitude on foil and survived a crash.

name: Paralyzing drug or venom
milestone: Harold Griffith and Enid Johnson gave a standardized curare preparation to a patient during an appendectomy.

name: Giant or supposedly extinct birds surviving in remote lands
milestone: Geoffrey Orbell's expedition rediscovered the South Island takahe, presumed extinct since 1898, alive in an isolated valley of the Murchison Mountains, New Zealand.

best_entry.title: A Strange Manuscript Found in a Copper Cylinder

name: Large power switch
reasons: best entry of a top-100 author
best entry of a top-100 book
milestone: ABB announced a hybrid HVDC breaker combining fast mechanics with power electronics, interrupting power flows of a large power station within 5 ms.

name: Magnetic levitation train
reasons: best entry of a top-100 book
milestone: The Birmingham Maglev people mover opened as the first commercial maglev service between airport and station.

name: Battery-powered spacecraft
milestone: NASA Lewis flew SERT-1 on a suborbital rocket; its mercury electron-bombardment ion thruster, run from a battery, operated in space for 31 minutes and thrust was measured.

name: Robot combat sport
reasons: best entry of a top-100 book
milestone: Same event: an actual held robot combat competition.

name: Space weather forecasting
milestone: The Space Disturbances Laboratory of the Central Radio Propagation Laboratory (ESSA, Boulder) began issuing daily space weather forecasts to the public.

name: Robot mannequin
reasons: best entry of a top-100 book
milestone: Flower Robotics (Tatsuya Matsui, with SGI Japan) unveiled Palette at a Tokyo press event: a powered female mannequin that replays supermodel motion-capture poses and poses for the nearest passing shopper to show off the clothes it wears.

name: Credit card payment
milestone: Diners Club began issuing cards to members, who signed restaurant tabs at 200 restaurants and clubs in six cities by late 1950.

name: Skip reentry
reasons: best entry of a top-100 author
milestone: The Soviet Zond 6 lunar-circling capsule returned using a skip reentry: it dipped into the upper atmosphere, climbed back out and re-entered, limiting deceleration to 4-7 g.

name: Vertical farm
milestone: Sky Greens opened in Singapore, billed as the world's first commercial vertical farm, with 100+ nine-metre towers.

name: Electronic location tracking of people
reasons: best entry of a top-100 book
milestone: Judge Jack Love persuaded Michael Goss to found NIMCOS, which built radio ankle transmitters used to monitor offenders from a telephone-linked receiver.
